body:
> we could have a "Copy Project" project button on the side

Duplicate button is useful on its own when making a lot of small similar projects regardless of whether there are other ways to backup. It would close https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/2292

Besides that dialog with a "Make Backup First" checkbox that makes a copy and then upgrades and opens the original makes the most sense to me
I think using both (1) and (2) from alternative approaches would be great.
I often do this manually, it would be useful to have such a feature.
I'm also aligned with @passivestar and @arkology on going with (1) and (2) from the alternative approaches.

I've updated the PR with alternative approaches nr 1 and 2, which means:

- Using a "Backup project first" checkbox (rather than an additional button)
- Adding a "Duplicate" button to the right sidebar, so users can duplicate arbitrary projects

I've updated the PR description with new screenshots showing all these changes!

Note: I looked at adding a progress dialog, but noticed that we are currently just freezing when installing a project from a ZIP file too, so doing the same for project duplication wouldn't be any worse. We probably should have a progress dialog here for both installing from ZIP and project duplication, but since this matches pre-existing behavior, it seems like something that can be handled in a future PR

So, taking this one out of DRAFT - it's ready for review :-)

The duplicate option, or at least the backup one, should try to create the duplicate in the same directory as original. Right now it uses default project path.

Also I noticed that making project's backup/duplicate will change its name and directory name. Shouldn't they stay the same? The project name could be as is, the directory name could be `Original Directory Name (Copy)`, instead of using project's name like when creating new project.

@KoBeWi Thanks for the review!

> The duplicate option, or at least the backup one, should try to create the duplicate in the same directory as original. Right now it uses default project path.

Added in my latest push!

> Project manager crashes if you try to duplicate a project that was removed externally while the manager was open

Eep! Thanks for catching that :-)

Fixed in my latest push

> Also I noticed that making project's backup/duplicate will change its name and directory name. Shouldn't they stay the same? The project name could be as is, the directory name could be `Original Directory Name (Copy)`, instead of using project's name like when creating new project.

Personally, I like being able to change the project name of the duplicate in that dialog.

Especially when doing a backup due to a version update, because you aren't going to open that project in the editor to rename it (otherwise it'd get updated) and this makes it easier to recognize in the project manager. But even when using the "Duplicate" button in the right sidebar, it prevents you from forgetting to change it when editing the project, avoiding future confusion in the project manager.
